text: 3412 Kafka, with the provisional designation 1983 AU2, is an asteroid located in the inner regions of the asteroid belt and is approximately 6 kilometers in diameter. It was discovered on 10 January 1983 by American astronomers Randolph Kirk and Donald Rudy at Palomar Observatory in California, United States. The asteroid was first identified as 1942 YB at the Finnish Turku Observatory in 1942, extending its observation arc by 41 years before its official discovery. It orbits the Sun in the inner main belt at a distance of 2.0–2.5 AU, completing one orbit every 3 years and 4 months (1,212 days), with an orbital eccentricity of 0.10 and an inclination of 3° relative to the ecliptic. According to data from NASA's Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer and its NEOWISE mission, Kafka has a diameter of 6.1 kilometers and a surface albedo of 0.231. It is classified as a superslow rotator, with a rotation period of 2,766 hours (about 115 days), which is among the longest known for any asteroid. The asteroid was named after Franz Kafka (1883–1924), the Austrian–Czech writer known for novels and short stories in which protagonists encounter bizarre or surrealistic situations. The official naming citation was published by the Minor Planet Center on 13 February 1987 (M.P.C. 11641).
